title: Are we there yet? A reality check on six big tech promises
text:
ARE

There are some seemingly impossible feats too good to give up on. Decoding a pet’s yowls and yips? Yes, please. Scrubbing the world of forever chemicals? Absolutely. Rocketing to Mars in a fraction of the time? Sounds great, but ...

WE THERE

EXPLORE MORE
IMPOSSIBLEIDEAS

YET?

REPORTING BY

Robin George Andrews, Cassandra Willyard, Sara Kiley Watson, and Alexander C. Kaufman

ILLUSTRATIONS BY SAM GREEN AND EOIN RYAN

We ran progress reports on six potentially transformative technologies and ideas that have been “just around the corner” for years or, in some cases, decades. We called up experts with a bird’s-eye view of the fields to get a sense of what’s holding things back, and we chatted with folks running the studies, crunching the data, and building the prototypes that could make these dreams into realities. Then we placed each idea on a progress meter ranging from 0 to 10—0 being “We don’t even know where to begin” and 10 being “We did it!” Check out the stories below to see how they all stacked up. Nuclear-powered spaceshipsA new era of spaceflight could save astronauts time and cut exposure to cosmic radiation as they rocket to Mars—and beyond.Exercise in a pillIn unraveling the pathways by which movement helps the body, we could develop medicines that offer some of the same benefits, without the workout.Interspecies communicationDecoding how animals communicate could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world.Solid-state batteriesBatteries that swap liquid electrolytes for solid materials promise to charge faster, last longer, and (crucially) run cooler.Cleaning up PFASRidding the world of forever chemicals could address a range of health and environmental woes for both people and planet.Eliminating traffic deathsDeploying simple, proven methods for making our roads safer could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.
